key_insight: PI-GINOT learns geometry-conditioned hyperelastic responses directly from specimen boundaries, eliminating the need for finite-element training data while still enforcing physics constraints.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster virtual testing and design studies for parametric solid structures like DogBone specimens when repeated nonlinear simulations would be too expensive.
method: Encodes each specimen’s boundary point cloud into geometry features.
Uses a cross-attention decoder to predict displacement at arbitrary interior points.
Enforces boundary conditions exactly and computes stresses via automatic differentiation with physics-informed losses.
evidence_signal: Validated on eight unseen geometries, the model reported displacement errors of 2.1%–7.1%, peak von Mises stress errors of 0.9%–13.3%, and section-force errors below 10.3% after training without FE labels.
watch_item: Local stress components remain less accurate, especially near gauge-to-fillet transitions in narrow specimens where stress gradients are steep.
paper_title: PI-GINOT: Data-free geometry-informed neural operator learning for finite-strain hyperelasticity on parametric DogBone specimens
